questions.solution: A patient is hooked up to a monitoring machine that shows voltage traces on a screen and makes the sound “... pip... pip... pip..... peeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee” as the patient goes into cardiac arrest. This type of machine (electro-cardiograph) is used to obtain an electrocardiogram (ECG). ECG is a graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart during a cardiac cycle. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Identify the A and B and then mark the correct statement.
options: B is an artery which carries oxygenated blood only.
A is a vein which carries deoxygenated blood.
A and B contain three layers of blood vessels.
questions.solution: A is vein and B is artery. Pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from lungs to heart. Blood vessels contain three linings (not layers)- Tunica externa, tunica media and tunica intima. Lumen is more in veins as it has thin tunica media. The blood flows strictly by a fixed route through Blood Vessels-the arteries and veins. Basically, each artery and vein consists of three layers: an inner lining of squamous endothelium, the tunica intima, a middle layer of smooth muscle and elastic fibres, the tunica media, and an external layer of fibrous connective tissue with collagen fibres, the tunica externa. The tunica media is comparatively thin in the veins. As mentioned earlier, the blood pumped by the right ventricle enters the pulmonary artery, whereas the left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta. The deoxygenated blood pumped into the pulmonary artery is passed on to the lungs from where the oxygenated blood is carried by the pulmonary veins into the left atrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Heart ValveLocation
A. Tricuspid Valve1. At the opening of the pulmonary artery
B. Bicuspid Valve2. Between right atrium and right ventricle
C. Pulmonary Valve3. Between left atrium and left ventricle
D. Aortic Valve4. At the opening of the aorta
questions.solution:
Tricuspid Valve is located between the right atrium and right ventricle, preventing the backflow of blood into the atrium during ventricular contraction.
Bicuspid Valve (Mitral Valve) is situated between the left atrium and left ventricle, allowing blood to flow from the atrium to the ventricle without regurgitation.
Pulmonary Valve is positioned at the opening of the pulmonary artery, controlling the flow of deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.
Aortic Valve is found at the opening of the aorta, regulating the flow of oxygenated blood from the left ventricle into the aorta.

questions.solution:

Closed Circulatory System: In a closed circulatory system, blood is always enclosed within blood vessels, which allows for more efficient transport of nutrients and gases
Single Circulation: In single circulation, blood passes through the heart only once during each complete circuit of the body. Double Circulation: In double circulation, blood passes through the heart twice during each complete circuit of the body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:

A. Fibrinogen1. Forms a mesh to stabilize the clot
B. Thrombin2. Converts into thrombin
C. Prothrombin3. Converts fibrinogen to fibrin
D. Calcium ions4. Required for several clotting steps
questions.solution:
Fibrinogen is a soluble protein that, when activated, forms fibrin, which creates a mesh-like structure to stabilize the blood clot.
Thrombin is an enzyme that plays a crucial role in blood clotting by converting fibrinogen to fibrin. Prothrombin is an inactive precursor of thrombin. During the clotting process, it is converted into thrombin, which then catalyzes the conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin.
Calcium ions are essential for several steps in the blood coagulation process.

Eosinophils are involved in the body's immune response to allergies and parasitic infections. Basophils release histamine, which contributes to inflammation and allergic responses.
Lymphocytes, particularly B cells, are responsible for antibody production.

Blood Group O is the universal donor but can only receive blood from O type due to the lack of A and B antigens.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:

A. Right Atrium1. Receives deoxygenated blood from the body
B. Left Atrium2. Pumps blood to the lungs
C. Right Ventricle3. Receives oxygenated blood from the lungs 4. Pumps blood to the systemic circulation
D. Left Ventricle4. Pumps blood to the systemic circulation
questions.solution:
Right Atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body through the superior and inferior vena cavae.
Left Atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins.
Right Ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation via the pulmonary artery.
Left Ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the systemic circulation, delivering it to the rest of the body through the aorta.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:

A. Systemic Circulation1. Heart to lungs and back
B. Pulmonary Circulation2. Gastrointestinal tract to liver
C. Hepatic Portal Circulation3. Heart to body and back
D. Coronary Circulation4. Heart to heart tissue and back
questions.solution:
Systemic Circulation involves blood traveling from the heart to the body and back, delivering oxygen and nutrients to tissues and returning deoxygenated blood to the heart.
Pulmonary Circulation carries blood from the heart to the lungs and back for oxygenation and removal of carbon dioxide.
Hepatic Portal Circulation refers to blood flow from the gastrointestinal tract to the liver, allowing the liver to process nutrients and toxins.
Coronary Circulation supplies blood to the heart tissue itself, ensuring it receives adequate oxygen and nutrients for proper function.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Cardiovascular DiseaseDescription
A. Angina Pectoris1. Chest pain due to reduced blood flow
B. Heart Failure2. Inability of the heart to pump blood effectively
C. Stroke3. Narrowing of arteries in the limbs
D. Peripheral Artery Disease4. Blockage of blood supply to the brain
questions.solution:
Angina Pectoris is characterized by chest pain due to reduced blood flow to the heart muscle, often caused by coronary artery disease.
Heart Failure refers to the inability of the heart to pump blood effectively, leading to symptoms such as shortness of breath and fluid retention.
Stroke occurs when there is a blockage of blood supply to the brain, resulting in damage to brain cells and potential loss of function.
Peripheral Artery Disease involves the narrowing of arteries in the limbs, reducing blood flow and causing symptoms like leg pain and cramping.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Heart SoundCause
A. First Heart Sound (S1)1. Rapid filling of ventricles
B. Second Heart Sound (S2)2. Closure of tricuspid and mitral valves
C. Third Heart Sound (S3)3. Atrial contraction
D. Fourth Heart Sound (S4)4. Closure of aortic and pulmonary valves
questions.solution:
First Heart Sound (S1) is caused by the closure of the tricuspid and mitral valves, marking the beginning of systole.
Second Heart Sound (S2) occurs due to the closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves, indicating the end of systole and the start of diastole.
Third Heart Sound (S3) is produced by the rapid filling of ventricles during early diastole, often associated with heart failure or high cardiac output.
Fourth Heart Sound (S4) results from atrial contraction just before the S1 sound, indicating increased resistance to ventricular filling, often seen in conditions like hypertension.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:

B. Diastole2. Relaxation phase of the heart
C. Isovolumetric Contraction3. Ventricles relax with no volume change
D. Isovolumetric Relaxation4. Ventricles contract with no volume change
questions.solution:
Systole is the contraction phase of the heart, during which the ventricles contract to pump blood out of the heart.
Diastole is the relaxation phase of the heart, during which the heart chambers relax and fill with blood.
Isovolumetric Contraction occurs when the ventricles contract with no volume change, as the valves are closed and pressure builds up before ejection.
Isovolumetric Relaxation happens when the ventricles relax with no volume change, as all valves are closed and the pressure decreases before the chambers refill.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The mitral valve in the human heart functions primarily to prevent the backflow of blood:
options: from the left atrium into the left ventricle
from the left ventricle into the left atrium
from the right ventricle into the right atrium
from the aorta into the left ventricle
questions.solution:
The mitral valve, also known as the bicuspid valve, guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle.

During ventricular systole (contraction), the pressure inside the left ventricle increases. The mitral valve closes to prevent the backflow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium.

Blood flowing from the left atrium to the left ventricle is the normal forward flow, not backflow. The tricuspid valve prevents backflow from the right ventricle to the right atrium, and the semilunar valves prevent backflow from the aorta and pulmonary artery into the ventricles.

Answer: from the left ventricle into the left atrium

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A patient's blood report indicates an absolute basophil count of $40 - 80$ cells/cu.mm. Assuming this represents the normal healthy percentage range for basophils, what would be the expected absolute number of neutrophils in the same volume of blood?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, basophils constitute $0.5 - 1\%$ of the total WBCs.

Given the absolute basophil count is $40 - 80$ cells/cu.mm, we can determine the total WBC count.
If $0.5 - 1\%$ corresponds to $40 - 80$ cells, then $1\%$ corresponds to $80$ cells.
Total WBC count = $80 \times 100 = 8000$ cells/cu.mm.

Neutrophils constitute $60 - 65\%$ of the total WBCs.

Expected number of neutrophils = $\dfrac{60}{100} \times 8000$ to $\dfrac{65}{100} \times 8000$
$= 4800 - 5200$ cells/cu.mm.

Calculating the lymphocyte count ($20 - 25\%$) would yield $1600 - 2000$ cells/cu.mm, which is an incorrect distractor. Assuming a standard total WBC count of $10000$ without calculating from the given data leads to $6000 - 6500$ cells/cu.mm.

Answer: $4800 - 5200$ cells/cu.mm

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Bone marrow and thymus are classified as primary lymphoid organs.

Reason (R) : In bone marrow and thymus, immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

The defining characteristic of primary lymphoid organs is that they are the sites where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes. In humans, the bone marrow and thymus serve this exact function, which is the reason they are classified as primary lymphoid organs.

After maturation, these antigen-sensitive lymphocytes migrate to secondary lymphoid organs.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A man with blood group O and a woman with blood group AB cannot have a child with blood group AB or blood group O.

Reason (R): The allele for blood group O ($i$) is recessive, and since the child inherits exactly one allele from each parent, all offspring of this couple will be obligate heterozygotes for either blood group A or B.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
The man has blood group O, so his genotype must be $ii$. He can only produce gametes carrying the $i$ allele.

The woman has blood group AB, so her genotype must be $I^A I^B$. She can produce gametes carrying either the $I^A$ or $I^B$ allele.

Since a child inherits exactly one allele from each parent, every child of this couple will receive an $i$ allele from the father and either an $I^A$ or $I^B$ allele from the mother. This results in the offspring having genotypes $I^A i$ (Blood group A) or $I^B i$ (Blood group B).

Because the $i$ allele is recessive to both $I^A$ and $I^B$, the children will express either blood group A or B. They are obligate heterozygotes. They cannot have blood group O ($ii$) because the mother does not have an $i$ allele to contribute. They cannot have blood group AB ($I^A I^B$) because the father does not have an $I^A$ or $I^B$ allele to contribute.

Thus, the Assertion is correct, and the Reason provides the correct genetic explanation for it.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are five events related to blood coagulation and formed elements.

(A) Conversion of inactive fibrinogens to fibrins
(B) Formation of the enzyme complex thrombokinase
(C) Trapping of dead formed elements which are normally destroyed in the spleen
(D) Conversion of prothrombin to thrombin
(E) Release of certain factors by injured tissues and platelets

Choose the correct sequential order of these events from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The mechanism of blood coagulation proceeds in a specific cascade:

First, an injury stimulates platelets and tissues at the site to release certain factors (E).
These factors initiate a cascade of enzymic reactions leading to the formation of the enzyme complex thrombokinase (B).
Thrombokinase then catalyzes the conversion of inactive prothrombin in the plasma into the active enzyme thrombin (D).
Thrombin, in turn, converts inactive fibrinogens into fibrins (A).
Finally, fibrins form a network of threads that trap dead and damaged formed elements (C), such as erythrocytes (RBCs), which are otherwise normally destroyed in the spleen (the graveyard of RBCs).

Thus, the correct sequential order is (E) \rightarrow (B) \rightarrow (D) \rightarrow (A) \rightarrow (C).

Answer: (E), (B), (D), (A), (C)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding erythroblastosis foetalis:
(A) It occurs due to Rh incompatibility between an Rh-negative mother and an Rh-positive foetus.
(B) The maternal immune system is typically exposed to the foetal Rh antigen during the first trimester of the first pregnancy.
(C) The condition leads to severe anaemia and jaundice in the affected baby.
(D) It can be prevented by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as erythroblastosis foetalis is a special case of Rh incompatibility between an Rh-negative mother and an Rh-positive foetus.

Statement (B) is incorrect because the foetal and maternal blood are normally kept well separated by the placenta during pregnancy. Exposure to the Rh antigen typically occurs at the time of birth of the first child, not during the first trimester.

Statement (C) is correct as the destruction of foetal red blood cells by maternal antibodies causes severe anaemia and jaundice in the newborn.

Statement (D) is correct as the standard preventive measure is administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child to prevent maternal sensitization.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
At the site of an injury, a dark reddish-brown scum is formed that traps dead and damaged formed elements. The most abundant of these trapped elements have an average life span of 120 days and are destroyed in organ 'X'. The threads of this scum are formed from soluble plasma proteins by the action of an enzyme 'Y'.

Identify 'X' and 'Y'.
questions.solution:
The most abundant formed elements in blood are erythrocytes (RBCs), which have an average life span of 120 days. They are destroyed in the spleen, making 'X' the spleen.

The dark reddish-brown scum is the coagulum or clot, which is formed mainly of a network of threads called fibrins. These fibrins are formed by the conversion of inactive fibrinogens in the plasma by the enzyme thrombin, making 'Y' thrombin.

Fibrin is the structural thread itself, not the enzyme. Thrombokinase is the enzyme complex that activates prothrombin, not the one acting directly on fibrinogen. Bone marrow is the site of RBC formation, not destruction.

Answer: X - Spleen, Y - Thrombin

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A man with blood group AB marries a woman, and they have a child with blood group B. Which of the following genotypes cannot possibly belong to the mother?
questions.solution:
The father has blood group AB, so his genotype is $I^A I^B$. He can pass on either the $I^A$ or $I^B$ allele to his offspring.

The child has blood group B, which means the child's genotype must be either $I^B I^B$ or $I^B i$. Since the child must inherit one allele from each parent, and the father can provide the $I^B$ allele, the mother must provide either an $I^B$ allele (for an $I^B I^B$ child) or an $i$ allele (for an $I^B i$ child).

Therefore, the mother's genotype must contain at least one $I^B$ or $i$ allele. A mother with the genotype $I^A I^A$ can only pass on the $I^A$ allele. If she mates with an $I^A I^B$ father, the offspring can only be $I^A I^A$ (blood group A) or $I^A I^B$ (blood group AB). Thus, the mother cannot possibly have the genotype $I^A I^A$.

Answer: $I^A I^A$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the human immune system:

(A) Primary lymphoid organs provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen.
(B) Both B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes originate in the bone marrow.
(C) Spleen has a large reservoir of erythrocytes.
(D) Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue (MALT) constitutes about 20 percent of the lymphoid tissue in human body.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect because secondary lymphoid organs (like spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils) provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen, not primary lymphoid organs.

Statement (B) is correct as the bone marrow is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells, including both B and T lymphocytes, are produced.

Statement (C) is correct as the spleen acts as a filter of the blood and has a large reservoir of erythrocytes.

Statement (D) is incorrect because Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue (MALT) constitutes about 50 percent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body, not 20 percent.

Therefore, exactly two statements (B and C) are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a cubic millimeter of healthy human blood, platelets outnumber neutrophils.

Reason (R): The normal platelet count is $1,50,000-3,50,000\text{ mm}^{-3}$ while the total WBC count is only $6000-8000\text{ mm}^{-3}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. Platelets are present in the range of $1,50,000-3,50,000$ per $\text{mm}^{3}$ of blood. Neutrophils are the most abundant leukocytes, constituting $60-65\%$ of the total WBCs. Since the total WBC count is $6000-8000$ per $\text{mm}^{3}$, the absolute number of neutrophils is roughly $3600-5200$ per $\text{mm}^{3}$. Thus, platelets massively outnumber neutrophils.

Reason (R) is true and provides the correct mathematical basis for the Assertion. Because the entire WBC population is vastly smaller than the platelet count, any sub-population of WBCs (like neutrophils) must also be smaller than the platelet count. Therefore, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If the sino-atrial node (SAN) of a healthy individual generates exactly $75$ action potentials per minute, what will be the exact duration of a single cardiac cycle in this individual?
questions.solution:
The number of action potentials generated by the sino-atrial node (SAN) determines the heart rate, which is the number of heartbeats per minute.

Given that the SAN generates $75$ action potentials per minute, the heart beats $75$ times in $60$ seconds.

The duration of a single cardiac cycle is the time taken for one complete heartbeat.

Duration of one cardiac cycle = $\dfrac{60 \text{ seconds}}{75 \text{ beats}} = 0.80 \text{ seconds}$.

Dividing $75$ by $60$ incorrectly yields $1.25$ seconds. Assuming the standard average of $72$ beats per minute would incorrectly yield approximately $0.83$ seconds.

Answer: $0.80$ seconds

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A newborn baby is diagnosed with severe anemia and jaundice. Medical investigation reveals that the baby's red blood cells are being destroyed by antibodies that crossed the placenta from the mother's blood. Which of the following parental blood group combinations and maternal history most likely resulted in this condition?
options: Mother is Rh$^{-ve}$, Father is Rh$^{+ve}$; this is the mother's first pregnancy.
Mother is Rh$^{+ve}$, Father is Rh$^{-ve}$; this is the mother's second pregnancy.
Mother is Rh$^{-ve}$, Father is Rh$^{-ve}$; this is the mother's second pregnancy.
Mother is Rh$^{-ve}$, Father is Rh$^{+ve}$; this is the mother's second pregnancy.
questions.solution:
The condition described is erythroblastosis foetalis, which occurs due to Rh incompatibility between the mother and the foetus.

For this condition to occur, the mother must be Rh$^{-ve}$ and the foetus must be Rh$^{+ve}$. For the foetus to inherit the Rh antigen, the father must be Rh$^{+ve}$.

During a first pregnancy with an Rh$^{+ve}$ foetus, the Rh$^{-ve}$ mother is typically not exposed to fetal blood until the time of delivery, so the first child is usually unaffected. Sensitization occurs at birth, leading to the production of maternal anti-Rh antibodies.

In a subsequent (second) pregnancy with an Rh$^{+ve}$ foetus, these pre-formed maternal anti-Rh antibodies can cross the placenta and destroy the fetal RBCs, causing severe anemia and jaundice.

Thus, the mother must be Rh$^{-ve}$, the father Rh$^{+ve}$, and it must be a subsequent pregnancy for the antibodies to already be present and affect the foetus.

Answer: Mother is Rh$^{-ve}$, Father is Rh$^{+ve}$; this is the mother's second pregnancy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Neutrophils and monocytes both destroy foreign organisms entering the body and belong to the same main category of leucocytes.

Reason (R): Neutrophils possess specific granules in their cytoplasm, whereas monocytes lack these granules and have a kidney-shaped nucleus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is correct but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because although both neutrophils and monocytes are phagocytic cells that destroy foreign organisms, they belong to two different main categories of leucocytes. Neutrophils are granulocytes, while monocytes are agranulocytes.

Reason (R) is correct because neutrophils have granules in their cytoplasm (hence classified as granulocytes), whereas monocytes lack these granules (hence classified as agranulocytes) and possess a characteristic kidney-shaped nucleus.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is correct

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
(A) Spleen(I) Enzyme that converts inactive fibrinogens into fibrins
(B) Fibrin(II) Graveyard of RBCs
(C) Thrombin(III) Enzyme complex required for conversion of prothrombin
(D) Thrombokinase(IV) Network of threads trapping dead formed elements

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Spleen is known as the graveyard of RBCs.

Fibrins form a network of threads in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped.

Thrombin is the enzyme that converts inactive fibrinogens present in the plasma into fibrins.

Thrombokinase is the enzyme complex required to convert inactive prothrombin into active thrombin.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III). Swapping the roles of fibrin and thrombin or thrombin and thrombokinase are common points of confusion in the coagulation cascade.

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following couples has the potential to conceive a child who may suffer from erythroblastosis foetalis in a subsequent pregnancy?
questions.solution:
Erythroblastosis foetalis (Haemolytic Disease of the Newborn) occurs due to Rh incompatibility when an $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ mother carries an $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ foetus.

For the foetus to be $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$, the father must carry and pass on the $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ trait. The ABO blood group is irrelevant to this specific condition.

Looking at the options:
Option 1: Mother is $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ (no risk).
Option 2: Both parents are $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$, so the foetus will be $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ (no risk).
Option 3: Mother is $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ and Father is $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$. The foetus can be $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$, creating the necessary condition for erythroblastosis foetalis.
Option 4: Mother is $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ (no risk).

Thus, the couple with Mother $\text{O}^{-\text{ve}}$ and Father $\text{AB}^{+\text{ve}}$ is at risk.

Answer: Mother $\text{O}^{-\text{ve}}$ and Father $\text{AB}^{+\text{ve}}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Identify the most abundant agranulocyte and the least abundant granulocyte respectively from the options given below.
questions.solution:
Leukocytes (WBCs) are broadly grouped into two main categories: granulocytes and agranulocytes.

Agranulocytes include lymphocytes and monocytes. Lymphocytes constitute $20-25\%$ of total WBCs, while monocytes constitute $6-8\%$. Thus, the most abundant agranulocyte is the lymphocyte.

Granulocytes include neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils. Neutrophils are the most abundant ($60-65\%$), eosinophils are $2-3\%$, and basophils are the least abundant ($0.5-1\%$). Thus, the least abundant granulocyte is the basophil.

Neutrophil and Basophil is incorrect because neutrophil is a granulocyte, not an agranulocyte.

Answer: Lymphocyte and Basophil

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Leucocytes)List II (Characteristics/Functions)
A. NeutrophilsI. Inflammatory reactions and least abundant
B. BasophilsII. Immune responses of the body
C. EosinophilsIII. Most abundant and phagocytic
D. LymphocytesIV. Resist infections and associated with allergic reactions

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Neutrophils are the most abundant cells (60-65% of total WBCs) and are phagocytic in nature. (A matches III)

Basophils are the least abundant (0.5-1%) and are involved in inflammatory reactions by secreting histamine, serotonin, and heparin. (B matches I)

Eosinophils (2-3%) resist infections and are associated with allergic reactions. (C matches IV)

Lymphocytes (20-25%) are of two major types (B and T forms) and are responsible for the immune responses of the body. (D matches II)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

(A)Bone marrow(I)Small solid structures located at different points along the lymphatic system
(B)Thymus(II)Main lymphoid organ where all blood cells are produced
(C)Spleen(III)Lobed organ located near the heart and beneath the breastbone
(D)Lymph nodes(IV)Large bean-shaped organ that acts as a filter of the blood


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

Bone marrow is the main primary lymphoid organ where all blood cells, including lymphocytes, are produced.

Thymus is a lobed primary lymphoid organ located near the heart and beneath the breastbone.

Spleen is a large bean-shaped secondary lymphoid organ that acts as a blood filter by trapping blood-borne microorganisms.

Lymph nodes are small solid structures located at different points along the lymphatic system that trap microorganisms or other antigens entering the lymph.

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A patient is diagnosed with severe thrombocytopenia, a condition characterised by a significant decrease in the number of blood platelets. If this patient suffers a minor cut, which of the following steps of the blood coagulation cascade will be initially and most directly impaired?
options: Conversion of fibrin into fibrinogen at the site of injury
Direct conversion of soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads
Absorption of calcium ions by damaged tissues to form a clot
Release of factors that initiate the formation of thrombokinase complex
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, an injury or trauma stimulates the platelets (thrombocytes) in the blood to release certain factors which activate the mechanism of coagulation. These factors initiate a cascade of reactions leading to the formation of the enzyme complex thrombokinase.

A severe reduction in platelets (thrombocytopenia) will directly impair the initial release of these clotting factors, thereby preventing the formation of thrombokinase.

The conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin is a downstream event that fails because thrombokinase (and subsequently thrombin) is not formed. The conversion of fibrin to fibrinogen is biologically incorrect. Calcium is essential for clotting, but platelets do not absorb it to initiate the cascade.

Answer: Release of factors that initiate the formation of thrombokinase complex

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the nodal tissue of the human heart.

(A) The nodal musculature is autoexcitable and requires external stimuli to generate an action potential.
(B) The Sino-atrial node (SAN) generates the maximum number of action potentials, i.e., $70-75$ min$^{-1}$.
(C) The SAN is present in the right upper corner of the right atrium.
(D) The Atrio-ventricular node (AVN) is situated in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect because autoexcitable means the nodal musculature has the ability to generate action potentials without any external stimuli, not that it requires them.

Statement (B) is correct as the SAN generates the maximum number of action potentials ($70-75$ min$^{-1}$) and acts as the pacemaker.

Statement (C) is correct as the SAN is anatomically located in the right upper corner of the right atrium.

Statement (D) is correct as the AVN is located in the lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the atrio-ventricular septum.

Thus, exactly three statements (B, C, and D) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding secondary lymphoid organs is incorrect?
options: Peyer's patches of the large intestine act as secondary lymphoid organs.
Secondary lymphoid organs provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen.
After interaction with antigens, lymphocytes proliferate to become effector cells.
Lymph nodes serve to trap the micro-organisms which happen to get into the lymph and tissue fluid.
questions.solution:
Peyer's patches are located in the small intestine, not the large intestine. Therefore, the statement identifying them as part of the large intestine is incorrect.

Secondary lymphoid organs (such as the spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of small intestine and appendix) provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen, which then proliferate to become effector cells.

Lymph nodes are small solid structures located at different points along the lymphatic system that serve to trap the micro-organisms or other antigens, which happen to get into the lymph and tissue fluid.

Answer: Peyer's patches of the large intestine act as secondary lymphoid organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. First pregnancy with Rh$^{+ve}$ foetus in Rh$^{-ve}$ motherI. Nearly $80\%$ of humans
B. Subsequent pregnancy with Rh$^{+ve}$ foetus in untreated Rh$^{-ve}$ motherII. Administration of anti-Rh antibodies to the mother
C. Prevention of erythroblastosis foetalisIII. Severe anaemia and jaundice to the baby
D. Individuals having Rh antigen on their RBCsIV. Mother starts preparing antibodies against Rh antigen
V. Administration of anti-Rh antibodies to the baby

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A - IV, B - III, C - II, D - I
A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I
A - IV, B - III, C - V, D - I
A - IV, B - II, C - III, D - I
questions.solution:
During the first pregnancy, the maternal and foetal blood are well separated by the placenta, but exposure during delivery causes the mother to start preparing antibodies against the Rh antigen (A matches IV).

In subsequent pregnancies, if the mother is untreated, her Rh antibodies can cross the placenta and destroy foetal RBCs, causing severe anaemia and jaundice to the baby, a condition known as erythroblastosis foetalis (B matches III).

This condition can be prevented by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child, not to the baby (C matches II).

The Rh antigen is present on the surface of RBCs in nearly $80\%$ of humans (D matches I).

Answer: A - IV, B - III, C - II, D - I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A patient requires a blood transfusion. His parents have blood groups A and B, and his biological sister has blood group O. Blood tests reveal that the patient's plasma contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies. What is the patient's genotype and which blood groups can he safely receive?
options: $I^A I^B$ ; A, B, AB and O
questions.solution:
The patient's sister has blood group O (genotype $ii$), which means both parents must carry the recessive $i$ allele. Since the parents have blood groups A and B, their genotypes must be $I^A i$ and $I^B i$, respectively.

The patient's blood plasma contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies. According to the principles of blood groups, the absence of both these antibodies in the plasma is a characteristic of blood group AB. Therefore, the patient's genotype must be $I^A I^B$.

Individuals with blood group AB have both A and B antigens on their red blood cells and lack antibodies against them in their plasma. This makes them universal recipients. Hence, the patient can safely receive blood from donors of groups A, B, AB, and O.

Answer: $I^A I^B$ ; A, B, AB and O

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A blood sample from a person named 'X' is tested with different antisera. It shows agglutination with Anti-B serum and Anti-D (Rh) serum, but no agglutination with Anti-A serum. Which of the following groups of individuals can safely receive a blood transfusion from person 'X'?
questions.solution:
Agglutination with Anti-B serum indicates the presence of B antigens, and agglutination with Anti-D serum indicates the presence of Rh antigens. The lack of agglutination with Anti-A serum means A antigens are absent. Thus, the blood group of person 'X' is $\mathrm{B\ Rh}^{+}$.

A donor with $\mathrm{B\ Rh}^{+}$ blood can only donate to recipients who do not have anti-B antibodies and who can tolerate $\mathrm{Rh}^{+}$ blood. These compatible recipients are $\mathrm{B\ Rh}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{AB\ Rh}^{+}$.

Options with $\mathrm{Rh}^{-}$ recipients are incorrect because they would develop anti-Rh antibodies upon receiving $\mathrm{Rh}^{+}$ blood. Option 4 incorrectly lists the groups from which person 'X' can receive blood, rather than the groups to which they can donate.

Answer: $\mathrm{B\ Rh}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{AB\ Rh}^{+}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A doctor administers anti-Rh antibodies to a woman immediately after the delivery of her first child to protect her future pregnancies. Based on this medical intervention, what must be the Rh blood group status of the mother and her newborn?
options: Mother is Rh-positive and newborn is Rh-negative
Both mother and newborn are Rh-negative
Both mother and newborn are Rh-positive
Mother is Rh-negative and newborn is Rh-positive
questions.solution:
Erythroblastosis foetalis is a condition caused by Rh incompatibility when an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive foetus.

During the delivery of the first child, the maternal blood may be exposed to a small amount of the Rh-positive blood from the foetus. This exposure causes the mother's immune system to start preparing anti-Rh antibodies, which could cross the placenta and destroy the foetal red blood cells in subsequent pregnancies.

To prevent this sensitization, anti-Rh antibodies are administered to the Rh-negative mother immediately after the delivery of her Rh-positive child. This destroys any foetal Rh antigens in her bloodstream before her immune system can react to them.

Answer: Mother is Rh-negative and newborn is Rh-positive

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A woman with blood group O$^{-ve}$ is currently expecting her second child. Her first child was born with blood group A$^{+ve}$, and she did not receive any medical intervention (such as anti-Rh antibodies) after the delivery. Which of the following antibodies are most likely present in her blood plasma during this second pregnancy?
questions.solution:
Individuals with blood group O lack both A and B antigens on the surface of their red blood cells, so they naturally possess both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in their blood plasma.

The woman is Rh$^{-ve}$ and her first child was Rh$^{+ve}$. During the delivery of the first child, a small amount of fetal blood can enter the maternal circulation. Since she did not receive prophylactic anti-Rh antibodies immediately after delivery, her immune system recognized the Rh antigen as foreign and produced anti-Rh antibodies (a process called sensitization).

Therefore, during her second pregnancy, her blood plasma will contain her natural anti-A and anti-B antibodies, along with the acquired anti-Rh antibodies.

Answer: Anti-A, anti-B, and anti-Rh antibodies

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A blood clot or coagulum is mainly formed of a network of threads called fibrins.
Reason (R): The enzyme thrombin converts inactive fibrinogens present in the plasma into fibrins at the site of injury.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, a blood clot or coagulum is formed mainly of a network of threads called fibrins in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped. Thus, the Assertion is true.

Fibrins are formed by the conversion of inactive fibrinogens present in the plasma by the enzyme thrombin. Thus, the Reason is true.

The Reason correctly explains the Assertion because the enzymatic action of thrombin on fibrinogen is the exact biochemical mechanism that produces the fibrin network mentioned in the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding blood groups and their characteristics:

List-I (Blood Group)List-II (Characteristics)
(A) $\mathrm{AB\ Rh}^{-}$(I) Lacks A and B antigens but has Rh antigen on RBCs
(B) $\mathrm{O\ Rh}^{+}$(II) Has both A and B antigens but lacks Rh antigen on RBCs
(C) $\mathrm{A\ Rh}^{+}$(III) Has A and Rh antigens on RBCs, and anti-B antibodies in plasma
(D) $\mathrm{B\ Rh}^{-}$(IV) Has B antigen on RBCs, anti-A antibodies in plasma, and lacks Rh antigen

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Blood group $\mathrm{AB\ Rh}^{-}$ has A and B antigens on RBCs but lacks the Rh antigen. It has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies in plasma.

Blood group $\mathrm{O\ Rh}^{+}$ lacks A and B antigens on RBCs but has the Rh antigen. Its plasma contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies.

Blood group $\mathrm{A\ Rh}^{+}$ has A and Rh antigens on RBCs, and its plasma contains anti-B antibodies.

Blood group $\mathrm{B\ Rh}^{-}$ has B antigen on RBCs but lacks the Rh antigen. Its plasma contains anti-A antibodies.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Sino-atrial node (SAN) is called the pacemaker of the human heart.
Reason (R): The SAN can generate the maximum number of action potentials ($70-75$ per minute) among all nodal tissues.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
The Sino-atrial node (SAN) is a specialised patch of cardiac musculature that has the ability to generate action potentials without any external stimuli (autoexcitable).

Among all the nodal tissues, the SAN generates the maximum number of action potentials, which is $70-75$ per minute.

Because it generates the highest number of action potentials, it initiates and maintains the rhythmic contractile activity of the heart. For this reason, the SAN is called the pacemaker.

Therefore, both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains why the SAN acts as the pacemaker.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : The first Rh$^{+ve}$ child of an Rh$^{-ve}$ mother rarely suffers from erythroblastosis foetalis.
Reason (R) : The Rh antigens of the foetus do not get exposed to the Rh$^{-ve}$ blood of the mother in the first pregnancy as the two bloods are well separated by the placenta.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
Assertion is false, but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
The Assertion is true. Erythroblastosis foetalis typically affects subsequent Rh$^{+ve}$ pregnancies, while the first Rh$^{+ve}$ child of an Rh$^{-ve}$ mother is usually unaffected.

The Reason is also true and correctly explains the Assertion. According to NCERT, during the first pregnancy, the Rh antigens of the foetus do not get exposed to the maternal blood because the two blood supplies are well separated by the placenta. Sensitisation of the mother's blood generally occurs only during the delivery of the first child when maternal blood is exposed to small amounts of foetal blood.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following paragraph regarding the blood coagulation cascade and identify the correct option for the blanks A, B, C, and D.

An injury stimulates the formation of an enzyme complex [A]. This complex [A] is required to convert an inactive protein [B] into [C]. [C] in turn converts [D] into fibrins to form the clot.
options: A - Thrombin, B - Fibrinogen, C - Fibrin, D - Prothrombin
A - Thrombokinase, B - Prothrombin, C - Thrombin, D - Fibrinogen
A - Thrombokinase, B - Thrombin, C - Prothrombin, D - Fibrinogen
A - Thrombokinase, B - Prothrombin, C - Thrombin, D - Fibrin
questions.solution:
The coagulation of blood involves a cascade of enzymatic reactions.

An injury or trauma stimulates the formation of an enzyme complex called thrombokinase [A].

Thrombokinase is required to convert an inactive protein present in the plasma called prothrombin [B] into its active form, thrombin [C].

Thrombin [C] then acts as an enzyme to convert inactive fibrinogen [D] into fibrins, which form the network of the clot.

Therefore, A is Thrombokinase, B is Prothrombin, C is Thrombin, and D is Fibrinogen.

Answer: A - Thrombokinase, B - Prothrombin, C - Thrombin, D - Fibrinogen

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During the cardiac cycle, as ventricular systole is initiated, the pressure inside the ventricles increases. Which of the following sets of valves close immediately to prevent the backflow of blood into the atria?
questions.solution:
During the cardiac cycle, the initiation of ventricular systole causes ventricular pressure to increase.

This increased pressure forces the closure of the atrio-ventricular (AV) valves to prevent the backflow of blood into the atria. The AV valves are the tricuspid valve (located between the right atrium and right ventricle) and the bicuspid or mitral valve (located between the left atrium and left ventricle).

The semilunar valves close during ventricular diastole, not systole, to prevent backflow from the pulmonary artery and aorta into the ventricles.

Answer: Tricuspid and bicuspid valves

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ mother usually does not suffer complications due to Rh incompatibility during her first pregnancy with an $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ foetus.
Reason (R): The foetal and maternal blood are normally kept well separated by the placental barrier during pregnancy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because during the first pregnancy, the $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ mother is usually not exposed to the $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ antigens of the foetus.

Reason (R) is correct and correctly explains the assertion. The foetal and maternal blood are normally kept well separated by the placenta, preventing the mother's immune system from encountering the foetal Rh antigens and producing anti-Rh antibodies until the time of birth when the placenta detaches.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: To obtain a standard electrocardiogram (ECG) for continuously monitoring basic heart activity, a patient is connected to the machine with three electrical leads. What is the correct anatomical placement of these three leads?
options: One to each wrist and one to the left ankle
One to each ankle and one to the left wrist
One to the right wrist and one to the left ankle
Multiple leads attached only to the chest region
questions.solution:
To obtain a standard ECG, a patient is connected to the machine with three electrical leads: one to each wrist and one to the left ankle. This configuration continuously monitors the basic heart activity.

For a more detailed evaluation of the heart's function, multiple leads are attached to the chest region, but the standard baseline setup requires only the three specific limb leads. Swapping the placement (e.g., each ankle and left wrist) or missing a lead is incorrect.

Answer: One to each wrist and one to the left ankle

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the components of the blood coagulation cascade.

List-IList-II
A. FibrinogenI. Enzyme complex that activates prothrombin
B. ThrombinII. Soluble inactive protein in plasma
C. ThrombokinaseIII. Essential mineral ion for clotting
D. Calcium ionsIV. Enzyme that converts inactive precursor into fibrin

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, fibrinogens are soluble inactive proteins present in the plasma (A-II).

Thrombin is the active enzyme that converts inactive fibrinogen into fibrin threads (B-IV).

Thrombokinase is an enzyme complex formed by a cascade of reactions, which is required to convert inactive prothrombin into active thrombin (C-I).

Calcium ions play a very important role in the entire clotting cascade (D-III).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a standard electrocardiogram (ECG), which of the following specific points marks the end of ventricular systole?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the T-wave represents the return of the ventricles from an excited to a normal state (repolarisation). The exact point that marks the end of ventricular systole is the end of the T-wave.

The Q wave marks the beginning of ventricular systole, while the beginning or peak of the T-wave represents intermediate stages of repolarisation rather than the mechanical end of the contraction.

Answer: End of the T-wave

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
In a routine blood test, the differential leukocyte count of a healthy individual is represented by five variables based on their relative abundance:
A : $60-65\%$
B : $20-25\%$
C : $6-8\%$
D : $2-3\%$
E : $0.5-1\%$

Identify the types of leukocytes that correspond to variables C and E respectively.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the relative abundance of different white blood cells (leukocytes) is as follows:
Neutrophils: $60-65\%$ (A)
Lymphocytes: $20-25\%$ (B)
Monocytes: $6-8\%$ (C)
Eosinophils: $2-3\%$ (D)
Basophils: $0.5-1\%$ (E)

Therefore, variable C corresponds to Monocytes and variable E corresponds to Basophils.

Answer: Monocytes and Basophils

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a healthy individual with a total WBC count of $7000$/mm$^3$, the number of monocytes will be between $420$ and $560$/mm$^3$.

Reason (R): Monocytes are phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. Monocytes constitute $6 - 8\%$ of the total WBCs. For a total WBC count of $7000$/mm$^3$, the expected number of monocytes is calculated as $\dfrac{6}{100} \times 7000$ to $\dfrac{8}{100} \times 7000 = 420$ to $560$/mm$^3$.

Reason (R) is true. According to NCERT, neutrophils and monocytes are phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A) because it explains their function rather than their relative percentage in the blood, which is the actual basis for the numerical calculation.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The bicuspid valve is also known as the mitral valve and it guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle.
Reason (R): The mitral valve is formed of three muscular flaps or cusps.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.solution:
The bicuspid valve, also known as the mitral valve, guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle. Hence, the Assertion is correct.

The mitral valve is formed of two muscular flaps or cusps, not three. The valve formed of three muscular flaps is the tricuspid valve, which guards the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle. Hence, the Reason is incorrect.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A newborn baby suffers from severe anaemia and jaundice due to a condition known as erythroblastosis foetalis. For this condition to occur, what must be the Rh blood group status of the baby's parents?
questions.solution:
Erythroblastosis foetalis is caused by Rh incompatibility between an $\mathrm{Rh}^{-}$ mother and an $\mathrm{Rh}^{+}$ foetus. The foetus inherits the $\mathrm{Rh}^{+}$ trait from the father.

Therefore, the mother must be $\mathrm{Rh}^{-}$ and the father must be $\mathrm{Rh}^{+}$. If the mother were $\mathrm{Rh}^{+}$, she would not produce anti-Rh antibodies upon exposure to the foetal blood, and the condition would not occur. If both were $\mathrm{Rh}^{-}$, the foetus could not be $\mathrm{Rh}^{+}$.

Answer: Mother is $\mathrm{Rh}^{-}$ and Father is $\mathrm{Rh}^{+}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Consider a family where the father has both A and B antigens on his red blood cells, and the mother has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in her blood plasma. Read the following statements regarding their potential offspring:

(I) They can have a child with no antigens of the ABO group on their red blood cells.
(II) 50% of their children are expected to have anti-B antibodies in their blood plasma.
(III) All their children will be heterozygous for the ABO blood group gene.
(IV) They can have a child who is a universal recipient for blood transfusion.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The father has both A and B antigens on his RBCs, which means his blood group is AB and his genotype is $I^A I^B$.

The mother has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in her plasma, which means her blood group is O and her genotype is $ii$.

A cross between them ($I^A I^B \times ii$) will produce offspring who receive either the $I^A$ or $I^B$ allele from the father and the $i$ allele from the mother. Thus, the possible genotypes of the children are $I^A i$ (Blood group A) and $I^B i$ (Blood group B) in a 1:1 ratio.

Evaluating the statements:
(I) Incorrect. A child with no antigens would have blood group O ($ii$), which is not possible since the father does not have an $i$ allele to pass on.
(II) Correct. 50% of the children will have blood group A ($I^A i$). Individuals with blood group A have anti-B antibodies in their plasma.
(III) Correct. All children will have either genotype $I^A i$ or $I^B i$, both of which are heterozygous.
(IV) Incorrect. A universal recipient has blood group AB ($I^A I^B$), which is not possible because the mother can only pass on the $i$ allele.

Therefore, exactly two statements, (II) and (III), are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the relative abundance of different types of leucocytes in a healthy human.

List-IList-II
A. NeutrophilsI. $0.5 - 1\%$
B. BasophilsII. $60 - 65\%$
C. MonocytesIII. $2 - 3\%$
D. EosinophilsIV. $6 - 8\%$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, leucocytes are divided into two main categories: granulocytes and agranulocytes.

Neutrophils are the most abundant cells ($60 - 65\%$) of the total WBCs.

Basophils are the least abundant ($0.5 - 1\%$) among them.

Monocytes constitute $6 - 8\%$ of total WBCs.

Eosinophils constitute $2 - 3\%$ of total WBCs.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Swapping the percentages of Monocytes and Eosinophils or Neutrophils and Monocytes leads to the incorrect options.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following specialised cardiac musculatures has the intrinsic ability to generate the maximum number of action potentials without any external stimuli and is responsible for initiating the rhythmic contractile activity of the heart?
questions.solution:
The entire nodal musculature is autoexcitable, meaning it can generate action potentials without any external stimuli.

However, the sino-atrial node (SAN) generates the maximum number of action potentials, i.e., $70-75$ per minute. This makes it responsible for initiating and maintaining the rhythmic contractile activity of the heart, which is why the SAN is called the pacemaker.

The atrio-ventricular node (AVN), bundle of His, and Purkinje fibres also possess autoexcitability but have progressively lower intrinsic rates of action potential generation.

Answer: Sino-atrial node

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A laboratory analysis of a patient's blood sample reveals a total WBC count of $6000$/cu.mm. In this sample, 'Cell A' represents the most abundant phagocytic cells, while 'Cell B' represents the cells that secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin. What would be the approximate absolute number of Cell A and Cell B in the given blood sample?
questions.solution:
Total WBC count = $6000$/cu.mm.

According to NCERT, neutrophils are the most abundant cells ($60 - 65\%$) of the total WBCs and are phagocytic in nature. Thus, Cell A is a neutrophil.

Number of neutrophils (Cell A) = $\dfrac{60}{100} \times 6000$ to $\dfrac{65}{100} \times 6000 = 3600 - 3900$/cu.mm.

Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin, etc., and constitute $0.5 - 1\%$ of the total WBCs. Thus, Cell B is a basophil.

Number of basophils (Cell B) = $\dfrac{0.5}{100} \times 6000$ to $\dfrac{1}{100} \times 6000 = 30 - 60$/cu.mm.

Option 2 incorrectly calculates for monocytes ($6 - 8\%$) and eosinophils ($2 - 3\%$). Option 3 correctly identifies neutrophils but misidentifies Cell B as eosinophils. Option 4 contains calculation errors.

Answer: $3600 - 3900$/cu.mm and $30 - 60$/cu.mm, respectively

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Cell X and Cell Y are both phagocytic leucocytes that destroy foreign organisms entering the body. Cell X is a granulocyte, whereas Cell Y is an agranulocyte. What are the respective shapes of the nuclei of Cell X and Cell Y?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, neutrophils and monocytes are the phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body.

Cell X is a granulocyte, which identifies it as a neutrophil. Neutrophils are characterised by a multilobed nucleus.

Cell Y is an agranulocyte, which identifies it as a monocyte. Monocytes are characterised by a kidney-shaped nucleus.

Therefore, the respective shapes of the nuclei for Cell X and Cell Y are multilobed and kidney-shaped. Reversing the order or confusing them with eosinophils (bilobed), basophils (S-shaped), or lymphocytes (large round) leads to the incorrect options.

Answer: Multilobed and Kidney-shaped

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Tricuspid valve(I) Lower left corner of right atrium
(B) Bicuspid valve(II) Base of pulmonary artery and aorta
(C) Semilunar valve(III) Opening between right atrium and right ventricle
(D) AV node(IV) Opening between left atrium and left ventricle

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The tricuspid valve guards the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle (A-III).

The bicuspid (or mitral) valve guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle (B-IV).

The semilunar valves are located at the openings of the right and left ventricles into the pulmonary artery and the aorta, respectively (C-II).

The atrio-ventricular node (AVN) is a mass of specialized tissue seen in the lower left corner of the right atrium (D-I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Thrombin is an active enzyme that converts inactive fibrinogens in the plasma into fibrins.
Reason (R): The coagulum formed at the site of an injury is mainly composed of a network of thrombin threads.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is a true statement. During blood coagulation, thrombin acts as the active enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of inactive soluble fibrinogens present in the plasma into insoluble fibrins.

Reason (R) is a false statement. The dark reddish-brown scum or coagulum formed at the site of an injury is mainly composed of a network of fibrin threads, not thrombin threads. Thrombin is merely the enzyme that facilitates their formation.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the standard electrocardiogram (ECG) and the cardiac cycle:
A. The P-wave represents the electrical excitation of the atria.
B. Ventricular contraction starts shortly after the Q wave.
C. The T-wave represents the depolarisation of the ventricles.
D. By counting the number of QRS complexes that occur in a given time period, one can determine the heart beat rate of an individual.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: The P-wave represents the electrical excitation (or depolarisation) of the atria, which leads to the contraction of both the atria.

Statement B is correct: The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates the ventricular contraction. The contraction starts shortly after Q and marks the beginning of the systole.

Statement C is incorrect: The T-wave represents the return of the ventricles from an excited to a normal state (repolarisation), not depolarisation.

Statement D is correct: Since each QRS complex represents one ventricular depolarisation (which corresponds to one heart beat), counting the number of QRS complexes in a given time period gives the heart beat rate.

Therefore, exactly three statements (A, B, and D) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A person with blood group $\mathrm{AB\ Rh}^{+}$ can receive a blood transfusion from any other blood group.
Reason (R): The plasma of a person with blood group $\mathrm{AB\ Rh}^{+}$ lacks anti-A, anti-B and anti-Rh antibodies.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion is true because individuals with blood group $\mathrm{AB\ Rh}^{+}$ are considered universal recipients and can safely receive blood from any ABO and Rh blood type.

Reason is also true and correctly explains the Assertion. The ability to receive any blood type is due to the complete absence of anti-A, anti-B, and anti-Rh antibodies in their blood plasma. If these antibodies were present, they would cause agglutination (clumping) of the donor's red blood cells.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II regarding the normal physiological abundance of formed elements in human blood.

List I (Formed Elements)List II (Abundance)
(A) Erythrocytes(I) $60-65\%$ of total WBCs
(B) Platelets(II) $20-25\%$ of total WBCs
(C) Neutrophils(III) $1.5-3.5$ lakh $mm^{-3}$
(D) Lymphocytes(IV) $5-5.5$ million $mm^{-3}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, a healthy adult man has, on average, $5$ millions to $5.5$ millions of RBCs (erythrocytes) $mm^{-3}$ of blood.

Blood normally contains $1,50,000-3,50,000$ platelets $mm^{-3}$.

Among leukocytes (WBCs), neutrophils are the most abundant cells ($60-65\%$ of the total WBCs) and lymphocytes are the second most abundant ($20-25\%$).

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding monocytes?

A. They are the most abundant white blood cells.

B. They are classified as agranulocytes.

C. They possess a kidney-shaped nucleus.

D. They secrete histamine and serotonin.

E. They are phagocytic cells that destroy foreign organisms.

Choose the correct answer from the options below:
questions.solution:
Leucocytes are divided into granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils) and agranulocytes (lymphocytes and monocytes). Thus, monocytes are agranulocytes (Statement B is correct).

Neutrophils are the most abundant WBCs (60-65%), whereas monocytes comprise 6-8% of total WBCs (Statement A is incorrect).

According to NCERT diagrams, monocytes have a kidney-shaped nucleus (Statement C is correct).

Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin, not monocytes (Statement D is incorrect).

Neutrophils and monocytes are phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body (Statement E is correct).

Therefore, the correct statements are B, C, and E.

Answer: B, C and E only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The heart beat rate of an individual can be determined by counting the number of QRS complexes in a standard ECG over a given time period.

Reason (R): The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates ventricular contraction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, by counting the number of QRS complexes that occur in a given time period, one can determine the heart beat rate of an individual.

This is because the QRS complex represents the electrical depolarisation of the ventricles, which leads to ventricular contraction. Ventricular contraction is the primary mechanical event that pumps blood out of the heart, corresponding to a single heartbeat.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.solution: Insulin decreases the level of glucose in the blood. It acts by stimulating liver cells and muscle cells to take up glucose from the blood and convert it into glycogen. When the blood sugar level drops, the secretion of insulin is suppressed. When the blood sugar level increases, the secretion of insulin is stimulated.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mature RBCs lose their ability for
options: Aerobic respiration, DNA replication and RNA synthesising machinery.
questions.solution: Matured mammalian RBCs do not have cell organelles including nucleus, Golgi bodies, mitochondria, ribosomes, centrioles and endoplasmic reticulum. It increases the surface area of RBCs and enables them to contain more haemoglobin. In the absence of cell organelles, the consumption of oxygen is very low and thus anaerobic respiration occurs in RBCs. Mature RBCs cannot replicate and cannot synthesise RNA as they do not possess machinery required (e.g., various enzymes) for replication and RNA synthesis.

questions.solution: Erythropoietin is a glycoprotein produced by the kidney, which regulates red blood cell formation in the bone marrow. During kidney damage, enough erythropoietin required for adequate RBCs production is not synthesised resulting in anaemia.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
A small rise in the body temperature of humans is corrected by
(i) sweating
(ii) dilating the skin arteries
(iii) constricting the skin arteries
(iv) increased tension of muscles in the skin.
questions.solution:
A small rise in body temperature is detected by sensory receptors in the skin and by special neurons, which monitor blood temperature, in the hypothalamus itself. When the neural centre of the hypothalamus involved in lowering body temperature receives information that body temperature is too high, it commands the arteries of the skin to dilate so that more blood, and therefore more heat, reaches the surface where heat can be lost.
A large rise in body temperature causes the hypothalamus to command both an extreme dilation in the arteries of the skin and the release of sweat from the body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Assertion : $\mathrm{ADH}$ and RAAS work in response to low blood volume and blood pressure.
Reason : ANF works in response to high blood volume and blood pressure.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Ifboth assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
ADH (Antidiuretic hormone) and RAAS (Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System) work in response to low blood volume and low blood pressure. ADH increases the reabsorption of water in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct, and thus results in an increase in blood volume and blood pressure. RAAS is operated by JGA (Juxtaglomerular apparatus). It increases blood volume and blood pressure by two ways: Firstly, it induces the proximal convoluted tubules to reabsorb more $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and water and secondly, it stimulates the adrenal gland to release a hormone, called aldosterone that induces the distal convoluted tubule to absorb more $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$and water.
ANF (Atrial Natriuretic Factor) works in response to high blood volume and high blood pressure. It opposes the regulation by RAAS. The walls of the atria of the heart release ANF in response to an increase in blood volume and blood pressure. ANF inhibits release of renin from the JGA and thereby inhibits $\mathrm{NaCl}$ reabsorption by the collecting duct and reduces aldosterone release from the adrenal gland. Thus ADH, RAAS and ANF regulate the functions of kidneys and control body fluid osmolarity, salt concentration, blood pressure and blood volume.

questions.solution: A normal electrogram (ECG) is composed of a P wave, a QRS wave (complex) and a $\mathrm{T}$ wave. The P-wave represents the electrical excitation or depolarisation of the atria. The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles which initiates the ventricular contraction. The contraction starts shortly after Q and marks the beginning of the systole. The T-wave represents the repolarisation of ventricles. The end of the T-wave marks the end of systole.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Assertion : On touching radial artery in our wrist, we feel pulse waves.
Reason : The heart beats originate from the sinoatrial node (SA node) on the right atrium.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
questions.solution: Pulse is the rhythmic contraction and relaxation in the aorta and its main arteries. It is a regular jerk of an artery. The pulse rate is exactly the same as the heart rate because an artery pulses every time the heart beats. Pulse is usually taken on the radial artery in the wrist but it can be taken on any artery that flows near enough to the surface of the body to be felt. The heart beat originates from the sinoatrial node (SA Node) - pacemaker, which lies in the wall of the right atrium near the opening of the superior vena cava. The SA node is a mass of neuromuscular tissue. Another mass of neuromuscular tissue, the atrioventricular node (AV node) is situated in the wall of the right atrium. The AV node picks up the wave of contraction propagated by SA node. A mass of specialized fibres, the bundle of His, originates from the AV node. The bundle of His divides into two branches, one going to each ventricle. Within the myocardium of the ventricles, the branches of bundle of His divides into a network of fine fibres called the Purkinje fibres. The bundle of His and the Purkinje fibres convey impulse of contraction from the AV node to the myocardium of the ventricles.

questions.solution: ABO blood groups are determined by the gene I (isoagglutinin). There are three alleles, $I^A, I^B$ and $I^O$ of this gene. Proteins produced by the $I^A$ and $I^B$ alleles are called $A$ antigen and $B$ antigen. People with blood group $A$ have the $A$ antigen on the surface of their RBCs, and antibodies against antigen $B$ in their plasma. Persons with blood group B have B antigen on their RBCs, and antibodies against $A$ antigen in their plasma. Individuals with $A B$ blood group have both antigen A and antigen $B$ on their RBCs, and no antibodies for either of the antigens in their plasma. Type $O$ individuals are without $A$ and $B$ antigens on their RBCs, but have antibodies for both these antigens in their plasma.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: You are required to draw blood from a patient and to keep it in a test tube for analysis of blood corpuscles and plasma. You are also provided with the following four types of test tubes. Which of these will you not use for the purpose?
questions.solution:
Clotting of collected blood can be prevented by -
coating test tubes with silicon (which produce non wettable surface similar in its smoothness to endothelial lining of blood vessels).
adding chelating agents (includes trisodium citrate, sodium oxalate and sodium EDTA) which remove calcium which is important for blood coagulation, and prevent blood clotting.
- adding heparin, most powerful anticoagulant which acts indirectly by activating plasma antithrombin III. Heparin is effective both in vivo and in vitro. Whereas the option $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}$ and $\mathrm{d}$ are effective in vitro.
Heparinized blood is not suitable for blood counts (as it alters the shape of RBC's and WBC's which affects blood testing), Fragility testing and complement fixation tests. Hence (c) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The component of blood which prevents its coagulation in the blood vessels is
questions.solution: Heparin prevents blood coagulation in the blood vessels. It is secreted by mast cells. It is an anticoagulant, blocking conversion of prothrombin to thrombin. Haemoglobin is the blood pigment necessary for oxygen transport. Plasma is the component of blood. Thrombin is the product of blood clotting.
